This occupation focuses on research and design of power and electrical systems in the electrical field, taking responsibility for design calculations and conformity conclusions; electronics engineers (except computer) focus on circuits and devices; engineering technologists and technicians provide design support and test records under engineering supervision, without independently approving designs.

Work context

Electrical engineers mainly perform office design work, organizing requirements, calculations and design, documentation, and verification support for projects, while also conducting site surveys and supporting construction and commissioning.
Workplaces: mainly offices, with surveys and support at factories, substations, or construction sites.
Main objects: electrical equipment, components, and systems, including distribution, protection, control, and drives.
Handoffs are needed with process, mechanical, construction, procurement, and supplier teams.
Working hours: most work full time, with more overtime at project milestones and during commissioning; site work requires prescribed protection.
Risks mainly arise from energized site environments, overlapping construction work, and neck and shoulder strain from prolonged desk work.
Tools and materials: design calculation and simulation software, drafting and documentation systems, standards libraries, and project management systems.

title.text: Electrical engineers: duties, wages, and entry paths

subject.name: Electrical engineers
subject.summary: Under U.S. O*NET-SOC 17-2071.00, research and design electrical equipment, components, and systems for commercial, industrial, military, or scientific use: organize requirements and applicable standards, complete electrical calculations and equipment selection, produce drawings and technical documents for checking, review, and signing, organize testing to verify conformity, and handle design changes.
